scope_note: First evidence-driven pass. Findings are limited to what was actually executed or read in this session. Absence of a finding in a category does NOT mean the category is clean — see NR-013 and the coverage matrix.

findings.title: Duplicate revision id made clinical_command_receipts unreachable
findings.description: Revision id 20260819_0003 was declared by two materially different migrations. Alembic resolved the id to the research-entities file, so the clinical_command_receipts migration was never reachable and never ran on any database.
findings.root_cause: Two migration files authored with the same revision identifier; Alembic silently resolves one and warns only.
findings.evidence: ScriptDirectory.get_revision('20260819_0003') resolved to 20260819_0003_research_entities.py; UserWarning 'Revision 20260819_0003 is present more than once'; table absent on every migrated database.
findings.affected_components: backend/migrations/versions, app/clinical/command_guard.py, all guarded clinical writes
findings.affected_users: Every clinician performing a guarded clinical command
findings.clinical_impact: Guarded clinical commands cannot execute at all on a correctly migrated database — the idempotency claim table is missing.
findings.security_impact: Idempotency/replay protection unavailable where the table is absent.
findings.data_integrity_impact: Duplicate clinical side effects possible if the guard is bypassed or the table is hand-created inconsistently.
findings.legal_impact: Audit/idempotency evidence unavailable for regulated clinical actions.
findings.recommended_fix: Unique revision identity for every migration; enforce in CI.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: Re-identified the migration as 20260908_0002 chained after 20260901_0004; research keeps 20260819_0003 because that is the id recorded on existing databases.
findings.verification_method: alembic heads; clean-database upgrade; table existence query; Blood Bank tests against the migration-built DB.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Unique revision ids; clinical_command_receipts created by migration alone.
findings.regression_risk: Low — no schema operation changed; an existence guard was added.

findings.title: Three unmerged heads made a clean deployment impossible
findings.description: The national-search, ICU-infusion and Blood Bank branches forked from the shared 20260814 lineage and never rejoined, so 'alembic upgrade head' could not choose a target and 'upgrade heads' reported an overlap.
findings.root_cause: Parallel feature branches merged into the repository without a corresponding Alembic merge revision.
findings.evidence: 'Multiple head revisions are present for given argument head'; 'Requested revision 20260819_0004 overlaps with other requested revisions 20260819_0003'; reproduced identically in CI job 102169201408.
findings.clinical_impact: No clinical function can run on a new deployment.
findings.data_integrity_impact: None directly; blocks schema creation entirely.
findings.operational_impact: P0: new environments cannot be built.
findings.recommended_fix: Merge revision; enforce single head in CI.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: Added merge revision 20260908_0001 with no schema operations.
findings.verification_method: alembic heads == 1; clean-database upgrade of the Blood Bank lineage.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Exactly one head; no duplicate-revision warning.
findings.regression_risk: Very low — merge carries no DDL.

findings.title: Pharmacy primary-key type divergence blocks any full upgrade head
findings.description: 20260716_0003 creates 23 pharmacy tables with Integer ids while 28 pharmacy ORM classes inherit a String(26) ULID primary key. 20260815_0023 therefore cannot build its foreign key and a full 'alembic upgrade head' still fails on a clean database.
findings.root_cause: Migration DDL and ORM model disagree on the pharmacy primary-key type; never detected because upgrade head could not run at all (NR-002 masked it).
findings.evidence: psycopg2.errors.DatatypeMismatch: Key columns 'original_drug_catalog_id' and 'id' are of incompatible types: character varying and integer (local run and CI job 102182712083). Counts: 23 Integer-id creates vs 28 ULID ORM classes.
findings.affected_users: All pharmacy users; and every deployment, since upgrade head cannot complete
findings.clinical_impact: Pharmacy dispensing/substitution cannot be deployed from a clean schema.
findings.data_integrity_impact: Severe: referential integrity between pharmacy entities cannot be expressed.
findings.recommended_fix: Decide the canonical pharmacy id type, then migrate all 23 tables and dependent FKs consistently.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: NONE ESTABLISHED — either direction is destructive and correctness cannot be derived from repository evidence. Requires an architecture decision.
findings.verification_method: Clean-database alembic upgrade head reaching the single head.
findings.acceptance_criteria: upgrade head exits 0 on an empty database.
findings.regression_risk: High — touches 23 tables and every dependent foreign key.

findings.title: Shared transition table shadowed the blood-unit reserved state
findings.description: _TRANSITIONS is one flat table shared by all Blood Bank entities and declared 'reserved' twice; the order entry silently replaced the unit entry, so reserved -> available and reserved -> released were rejected and a reserved unit could never return to the available pool.
findings.root_cause: Entity-agnostic state map keyed only by state name; duplicate key silently shadows.
findings.evidence: POST /blood-bank/reservations/{id}/release returned 422 'Invalid blood_unit transition: reserved -> available'; AST scan showed 39 keys / 38 unique.
findings.affected_users: Blood bank staff; patients awaiting units
findings.clinical_impact: Units stranded as reserved and withheld from the available pool — direct availability risk in transfusion.
findings.data_integrity_impact: Inventory state diverges from physical reality.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: Merged the two sets into one entry and removed the duplicate key.
findings.verification_method: Lifecycle E2E over real HTTP plus two unit regressions.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Reserve -> release returns the unit to available.
findings.regression_risk: Medium — merged set is the union, slightly wider for orders (residual, see NR-008).

findings.title: Unguarded duplicate index creation could never succeed
findings.description: 507ea11c820a re-created ix_lab_orders_lab_status_created without a guard although ancestor 20260503_0001 already creates it guarded.
findings.root_cause: Repository migration policy requires idempotent migrations; this one was authored without guards and never validated because upgrade head could not run.
findings.evidence: psycopg2.errors.DuplicateTable: relation 'ix_lab_orders_lab_status_created' already exists during clean upgrade.
findings.recommended_fix: Enforce the idempotency policy in CI for every new migration.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: Guarded both create_index calls; downgrade no longer drops the ancestor-owned index.

findings.title: Table national_facilities is mapped by two ORM classes on different bases
findings.description: app/models/clinical_scope.py::NationalFacility(Base) and app/national/domain/facility.py::Facility(AuditEntity) both map the physical table national_facilities.
findings.root_cause: Two domains modelled the same physical table independently; no ownership constitution enforced.
findings.evidence: AST scan of 828 mapped tables found exactly one table claimed by two app packages; both class definitions confirmed by reading.
findings.affected_users: Anything reading or writing facility data
findings.clinical_impact: Facility scoping underpins clinical authorization; divergent writes can misroute or mis-scope records.
findings.security_impact: Facility scope is an authorization input; two writers with different invariants weaken scoping.
findings.data_integrity_impact: Different column/audit expectations against one table; no shared invariants.
findings.operational_impact: Schema migrations may satisfy one mapping and break the other.
findings.recommended_fix: Declare a single owning domain; the other consumes via a read model or shared module.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: NOT ATTEMPTED — requires an ownership decision; changing either mapping risks silent behaviour change across authorization paths.
findings.verification_method: Ownership matrix plus a test asserting one ORM owner per physical table.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Exactly one writable mapping per physical table.

findings.title: Clinical state machine is entity-agnostic by construction
findings.description: transition(current, target, entity=...) uses 'entity' only for the error message; one flat dict governs blood units, orders, samples, crossmatches, transfusions and reactions. Any state name shared by two entity types collides.
findings.root_cause: No per-entity keying in the state machine design.
findings.evidence: app/blood_bank/domain/state_machine.py: _TRANSITIONS lookup ignores entity; NR-004 is a realised instance of the hazard.
findings.clinical_impact: A future duplicate state name silently widens or blocks a clinical transition, as already happened once.
findings.data_integrity_impact: Invalid transitions may be permitted across entity types.
findings.operational_impact: Fixes require union semantics that over-permit (current residual risk).
findings.recommended_fix: Key transitions by (entity, state) and fail closed on unknown entity.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: Deferred: NR-004 merged the colliding sets, which over-permits order transitions slightly.
findings.verification_method: Property-based test over every entity/state pair.
findings.acceptance_criteria: No transition is reachable for an entity type that does not define it.
findings.regression_risk: Medium — requires auditing every call site.

findings.title: signxml missing from requirements-lock.txt
findings.description: signxml>=4.2.0 is declared in backend/requirements.txt but absent from backend/requirements-lock.txt, so a lock-only environment cannot import app.security.saml_service.
findings.root_cause: Lock file regenerated without the SAML dependency.
findings.evidence: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'signxml' when installing from the lock file only; grep confirms presence in requirements.txt and absence in the lock.
findings.security_impact: SAML service unavailable in lock-only environments.
findings.operational_impact: Reproducible builds diverge from production image.
findings.recommended_fix: Regenerate the lock file from requirements.txt and gate drift in CI.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: Add the pinned signxml entry to the lock file.
findings.verification_method: pip install -r requirements-lock.txt then import the app.

findings.title: Artifact storage quota exhausted; every evidence job reports failure
findings.description: All iam-hardening jobs upload evidence artifacts; the account-wide GitHub Actions artifact storage quota is exhausted, so jobs fail at upload even when their tests pass.
findings.root_cause: Artifact retention/storage exceeded at account level.
findings.evidence: 'Failed to CreateArtifact: Artifact storage quota has been hit' on every backend job across four commits; security job shows '76 passed' immediately before the failing upload.
findings.operational_impact: CI cannot certify any change; red status is uninformative.
findings.recommended_fix: Free artifact storage or lower retention; separate evidence upload from pass/fail gating.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: Out of scope here (CI must not be modified in current phases).
findings.verification_method: A backend job completing without an upload error.

findings.title: if:always() evidence upload masks the true failing step
findings.description: The evidence upload step runs with if:always(), so a job whose real failure was an earlier step ends its log with the artifact-quota error. This caused the migration gate's genuine failure to be misread as a quota failure.
findings.root_cause: Log-tail inspection plus an always-run terminal step.
findings.evidence: Migration gate 102169201408 shows 'alembic ... FAILED ... exit code 255' followed by the artifact error; earlier commits were misclassified on that basis (including by this session, corrected).
findings.security_impact: Real failures can be dismissed as infrastructure noise.
findings.recommended_fix: Emit an explicit step-outcome summary, or make the upload non-failing (continue-on-error).
findings.minimal_safe_fix: Process rule: always classify CI failures by step sequence, never by the trailing error.
findings.verification_method: Triage checklist applied to a known mixed-failure job.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Job status distinguishes product / test / infrastructure failure.

findings.title: Mobile navigation button accessible name contradicts its test
findings.description: MobileBottomNav renders the menu button with aria-label 'More' and title 'Open all sections'. Accessible-name computation prefers aria-label, so the test querying 'Open all sections' can never pass.
findings.root_cause: Tooltip text mistaken for the accessible name.
findings.evidence: TestingLibraryElementError on two tests, reproduced on every commit; component sets both attributes.
findings.recommended_fix: Decide the intended accessible name; align component and test.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: Query by name 'More' in both assertions, or move the string into aria-label.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Tests reflect the intended accessible name.

findings.title: Replay returns a deterministic conflict, not the original response
findings.description: A completed command replayed under the same Idempotency-Key returns 409 with the canonical safe envelope; the original 2xx payload is not persisted or replayed, and the envelope hides whether the cause was replay or key reuse.
findings.evidence: Verified across Phase 14B/14B.1/14C: 409 CONFLICT with unchanged effect, movement and claim counts; discrimination observable only on the receipt.
findings.affected_users: API clients retrying after a lost response
findings.clinical_impact: Client cannot recover the original result and must re-read state.
findings.operational_impact: Clients need a documented read-after-conflict pattern.
findings.recommended_fix: Document the contract; consider stored-response replay only if clients require it.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: No change — behaviour is correct and proven.

findings.title: Audit coverage is narrow: most risk categories are unexamined
findings.description: This pass produced evidence for migration safety, Blood Bank clinical state, idempotency/concurrency, source-of-truth mapping and CI classification. The large majority of the 123 requested categories were not audited and must not be read as clean.
findings.root_cause: First audit pass under an explicit resource-minimisation rule.
findings.evidence: See the audit coverage matrix in GULA_MASTER_NEGATIVE_REGISTER.md.
findings.operational_impact: Certification cannot proceed on this evidence.
findings.recommended_fix: Run the audit category by category, each producing executed evidence.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: Publish the coverage matrix so absence of findings is not mistaken for absence of risk.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every category has a status and evidence link.

findings.title: No verified national capacity numbers exist
findings.description: No citizen, facility, throughput, storage or peak-load figures were found or established, so 'national scale' claims are unquantified.
findings.evidence: Not audited in this pass; recorded as a gap rather than an assumption, per instruction 18.
findings.operational_impact: Cannot size infrastructure or set SLOs.

findings.minimal_safe_fix: Record as a gap; do not provision infrastructure speculatively (Green GULA).

findings.description: The migration job's Postgres service logged 'FATAL: password authentication failed for user postgres' before the migration step; the job continued, so something tolerates it.
findings.root_cause: Unknown — possibly a health-check probe using different credentials.

findings.operational_impact: Noise that can hide genuine auth failures.

findings.minimal_safe_fix: Investigate alongside the pharmacy migration work.

findings.title: The changed-files quality gate reported PASS when MyPy had failed to execute
findings.description: scripts/quality_changed_files_gate.py printed '0 diagnostics' and PASS while MyPy exited 2 without analysing anything. Two causes combined: run_mypy parsed diagnostics regardless of the exit code, so a failed run contributed an empty list that read as clean; and execution_error_regression only fired when the head's error DIFFERED from the baseline's, which is never the case when both sides run in the same environment. A tool that never ran was certifying the change.
findings.root_cause: Zero diagnostics was treated as evidence of cleanliness without first establishing that the tool actually ran. The gate shelled out to a bare 'mypy' on PATH, which can resolve to an interpreter lacking the project dependencies MyPy must import to load its SQLAlchemy and Pydantic plugins.
findings.evidence: Reproduced at d9fdd988: the pre-fix gate printed 'baseline.mypy_changed: 0 diagnostics ... QUALITY_CHANGED_FILES_GATE: PASS' while returncode was 2 with "No module named 'sqlalchemy'". Post-fix the same comparison reports real counts (mypy_changed 170 -> 135) and PASS.
findings.security_impact: A green gate is evidence a reviewer relies on. Any type regression, including one weakening a security or tenant-isolation path, could pass unexamined.
findings.operational_impact: False confidence in the merge gate.
findings.intersections: Generalises beyond MyPy: any executable check whose empty output is read as success without first proving it ran.
findings.recommended_fix: Distinguish 'ran and found nothing' from 'did not run'. A failed run yields no diagnostics at all and blocks; an unmeasured baseline also blocks, because non-regression cannot be established against nothing.
findings.minimal_safe_fix: ToolResult.measured; diagnostics gated on successful execution for MyPy as they already were for Ruff; execution_blockers replacing execution_error_regression; a distinct BLOCKED status; and MyPy invoked through sys.executable -m so it runs in the same environment as the dependencies it imports.
findings.verification_method: scripts/tests/test_quality_changed_files_gate.py: exit 0 with no findings passes; exit 1 with findings is counted as a regression; exits 2, 3 and -11 yield no diagnostics and block, including when baseline and head fail identically.
findings.acceptance_criteria: No tool execution failure can produce a PASS.
findings.regression_risk: The gate now surfaces pre-existing execution failures that were previously silent. Verified not to affect CI: the local block was Python 3.11 failing to parse PEP 695 syntax in backend/app/clinical_gateway/contracts.py; CI runs 3.12 and the same run completes (confirmed under 3.13, exit 0).
findings.evidence_strength: STRONG (reproduced before and after, with regression tests)
